SUBJECT - Kelderby, the same town as the reference image, in the same hand. A cobbled square at the top of the town at the mountain's foot, a large Gothic cathedral on its east side and a timber-framed coaching inn, The Bell, on its west side; one broad main street stepping south down the slope in short flights of shallow steps to a long stone quay on the harbour; side lanes off it; a rocky headland east of the harbour with a cliff path to a tall white lighthouse; a grey Scottish courtyard castle on the mountain's summit, about eighty blocks above the square, reached by a long cobbled road zig-zagging up the mountain's flank. The town is dressed for its yearly Founders' Play: bunting and painted banners.

SCENE 1, NEAR VIEW - THE SQUARE, AT THE INN DOOR. Eye height on the cobbled square, a few steps from the inn's front door. In the foreground Hedda, a cheerful middle-aged innkeeper in an apron over a good dark dress with a pencil behind her ear, standing at the timber-framed inn's door with a clipboard of notes, beckoning the viewer in. A hanging inn sign with a bell on it. Behind her, across the square, the tall Gothic west front of the cathedral; benches and a well, a half-built wooden stage with a furled curtain frame being set up on the square, bunting overhead. Late afternoon, clear sky, golden sun low in the west.
request.style_note: Kelderby, a cheerful stone-and-timber harbour town on the slope below a castle mountain, on the afternoon of its yearly Founders' Play, drawn in the same hand throughout: warm painterly storybook concept painting, bright and friendly, clear sky, golden late-afternoon sun from the west, honey light on grey stone-brick walls and dark spruce and oak timber, dark slate-blue tile roofs, a deep blue sea, green turf and flower boxes of red poppies, blue cornflowers and white daisies, strings of bright festival bunting and painted banners strung across the streets for the play. Everything is massed from large squared blocks with flat faces and clean right angles so every form could be built block by block in Minecraft: the houses are rectangular stone boxes with timber upper storeys and steep gable roofs, the main street is a broad cobbled street stepping down the slope in short flights of shallow steps, the quay is a straight stone wall with square bollards. People, where any appear, are ordinary townsfolk in plain wool, linen and aprons, never armoured, never armed. Nothing glows but lanterns and windows. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, label, text or border.
